properties.statement:
TWO CAPABILITIES WERE MARKED `realized` ON PASSING UNIT TESTS, THE USER THEN FOUND FOUR BUGS IN THE PRODUCT, AND NOTHING IN THE LOOP HAD ASKED. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14, item 14 — and he filed the same thing again in his own 'Gaps (mine / process)' section, which is why it is recorded as a loop defect rather than only as his error.

HIS WORDS, item 14: 'I linked a passing unit Verification and marked the increment Capabilities realized. The user then found first-day, civil-vs-UTC, join-day-owed, and a cache miss. `realized` is a claim about THE THREAD, not about the running product. Nothing in the loop said \"realized at unit, unvalidated in the field.\"' And in his own gaps: 'I promoted two Capabilities to realized on unit tests before the user had clicked through. Should have left `in_progress` until the gate matched their account.'

⭐ THE CONCEPT IS NOT MISSING — THE PROMPT IS. The capability lifecycle already distinguishes `realized` from `verified`, and `reconcile_verification` exists precisely to feed real run outcomes back in. So nothing in the vocabulary failed. What failed is that an agent with a green unit test had no moment at which anything asked 'green where?' — and the answer he needed was already expressible.

WHY THIS IS A LOOP DEFECT AND NOT MERELY A MISTAKE: he identified it himself, unprompted, in the same document. An error a careful reporter catches on their own review is one the tooling could have caught at the moment it happened, and the cost of not catching it was borne by the user rather than by him.

CONNECTED, AND THE REASON IT IS WORTH FIXING TOGETHER: `dec:should-a-realizes-edge-say-that-nobody-checked-the-file-still-obeys-the-rule` (his item 5) asks the deeper version — a checksum says the file has not moved, never that it still implements the rule. THIS one is the same hole at the STATUS layer rather than the edge layer: `realized` says a thread is complete, never that the thing works where people use it. Both were reported by the same session, an hour apart, and neither was noticed as the other's sibling until now.

HIS OTHER SELF-REPORTED PROCESS GAPS, recorded because they are evidence about the loop rather than confessions: he widened an accepted Decision from a debugging hypothesis (see `fact:defect-an-accepted-decision-can-be-widened-by-an-agents-diagnosis`); he did not export the graph (see `fact:defect-the-export-was-skipped-because-the-instructions-imply-a-stop-that-is-not-needed`); he did not run detect-and-ask on 62 unsurfaced gaps and says so CORRECTLY — 'they were not the work'; and he did not install the loop nudge, calling `loop_status` by hand. THREE OF THE FOUR HAVE A TOOLING CAUSE RECORDED AGAINST THEM. The fourth — declining to detect-and-ask — was the right call and is recorded so a later reader does not treat it as debt.
